findings.title: Fallback locales are not loaded before cached translation lookup
findings.body: `translate` only loads `config.locale`, not the fallback locales configured in `FallbackLocaleList`. Outside `ApplicationController#set_locale` (background jobs, mailers, console, or translations before that filter) a key missing from the current locale will be looked up in fallback locales whose YAML files have never been loaded via the lazy-loading patch, so it returns a missing-translation string. Worse, the no-argument path stores that result in the LRU cache (`@cache.getset(k) { translate_no_cache(key).freeze }`), so the missing string stays cached under `key+locale` even after the fallback locale is later loaded, until eviction/reload. Fallbacks must be ensured-loaded inside `translate` (or the backend lookup) before computing/caching the value, and the cache must not persist results computed before fallback locales were loaded.

findings.title: Fallback loading is only wired into web requests
findings.body: The PR is described as server-side localization fallbacks, but `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only invoked from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Server-side code that sets `I18n.locale` and translates without going through this controller (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks, plugin background work) never loads the site-default/English fallback files, so with the lazy translation loader those fallbacks silently return missing translations there. The ensure-loaded step belongs in the shared translation path (e.g. `I18n.translate`/`load_locale` logic), not solely in a controller filter.

findings.title: Fallback lookup queries SiteSetting on every translation
findings.body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` is called by the I18n fallbacks backend on every translation lookup, and it calls `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` each time. That puts a site-setting lookup (backed by Discourse's setting provider/cache machinery) on the hottest possible path — the very path `translate_accelerator.rb` exists to optimize — and it also raises `NoMethodError` if `default_locale` is ever nil/blank (e.g. early boot or a cleared setting). The fallback chain should be computed without a per-lookup setting query, or at minimum memoized/guarded with a safe default such as `:en`.

findings.title: No tests cover the custom fallback chain or its lazy loading
findings.body: This PR introduces a custom `FallbackLocaleList`, replaces the Rails `config.i18n.fallbacks` mechanism, removes the standalone pluralization initializer, and adds `I18n.ensure_loaded!`, but adds no specs. There is nothing verifying that a key missing in the user locale falls back to the site default and then English, that fallback locale files actually get loaded under the lazy-loading patch (including outside controllers), or that pluralized fallback strings still work. Regressions in this global I18n behavior would only surface as missing-translation strings in production; add specs for the fallback order, loading, and a pluralized fallback lookup before merging.
